questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Advanced Pipe Design”?
options: Advanced Pipe Design means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Advanced Pipe Design removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Advanced Pipe Design should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Advanced Pipe Design helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Advanced Pipe Design helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Advanced Pipe Design is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Pure pipe behavior” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Pure pipe behavior” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Pure pipe behavior” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Pure pipe behavior” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Pure pipe behavior” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Pure pipe behavior” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Pure pipe behavior” under Advanced Pipe Design. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Advanced Pipe Design”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
